answer: The Saffire VI sample card contained four samples configured for four ignitions [paper:saffire6:p3.2]. Table 1 lists the Saffire VI tests as VI-2 (Two-Sided PMMA, 54.1 kPa, 31.0 mol % O2), VI-3 (One-Sided PMMA, 54.6 kPa, 30.3 mol % O2), and VI-4 (28.8 mol % O2, 55.2 kPa) [paper:saffire6:p3.2]. Saffire VI test 1 (Nomex) did not ignite and its conditions are not in Table 1 [limits:source:saffire_ices2024].

chunks.source: NTRS 20160001047 (O2 partial pressure vs concentration flammability), PDF p. 3
chunks.text: The STS and the currently in-design CEV have resided at the 30% O2 at 70.3 kPa (10.2 psia) point of the normoxic curve. The ISS aims to operate at the 21% O2, 101.4 kPa (14.7 psia) point of the curve. Nonetheless, it has obtained much of its data at 24.1% O2, 101.4 kPa (14.7 psia) conditions due to sinusoidal fluctuations of oxygen with a mean of 21% O2 seen on the ISS. Future long duration habitation modules might select to operate at lower pressure normoxic conditions to minimize time loss and health risk associated with frequent depressurizations when frequently exiting habitats. In addition, low pressure environments also provide structural design benefits for long-duration habitats. Use of Extravehicular Activity (EVA) suits is another scenario in which a reduced pressure environment is desired. Off-nominal

chunks.text: Saffire ICES-2024-365 gives: Per-test ambient pressure (kPa), O2 (mol %), air flow (cm/s), flow direction, material, for the 5 samples in Table 1 (p.3). It does not give: Table 1 lists only the samples 'considered in this paper' (IV-1, V-2, VI-2, VI-3, VI-4). Other Saffire I-V samples are not in it. Saffire VI test 1 (Nomex) did not ignite (p.4). Its conditions are not in Table 1, so it is not plotted. One flow speed only: 20 cm/s concurrent for every listed test. For the PMMA tests the flow was reduced at 1120 s (p.4); the reduced speed is not in Table 1. One O2 value per test (the set condition). No pre/post-burn split. Microgravity (orbiting Cygnus) only. No partial gravity. No extinction or flammability-limit data: every plotted test ignited and burned.

chunks.source: Flame Frontier habitat gap report: Spacesuit
chunks.text: Spacesuit target: 100% O2 at 29.6 kPa, partial gravity. 0 solid-material tests in this window. No solid-material test in our sources had O2 and pressure in 100% O2 at 29.6 kPa together. Closest solids: highest O2 31% (Saffire VI-2, 54.1 kPa); lowest pressure 54.1 kPa (Saffire VI-2, 31% O2). SSCE lists up to 70% O2, but every SSCE pressure is ≥101.3 kPa (range markers; pairing not given). No flammability boundary (where a solid stops burning) was measured in 100% O2 at 29.6 kPa. The only one in our data, BASS-II eq. 6.1 for PMMA rods, was measured at 101.3 kPa. No combustion test at partial gravity: every point on both panels is from microgravity. Challenge page: "there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI". Non-solid tests in 100% O2 at 29.6 kPa: 0 CFI-G gas flames, 0 FLEX liquid droplets. They do not close a solid-material gap.

chunks.source: NTRS 20160001047 (O2 partial pressure vs concentration flammability), PDF p. 2
chunks.text: 2 JOURNAL OF ASTM INTERNATIONAL Background To safely and successfully operate in enriched oxygen conditions, understanding material flammability is critical for NASA, commercial space flight companies, and industry alike. Previous space programs have acquired significant data in the Space Transportation System (STS) environment of 30% O2 at 70.3 kPa (10.2 psia). This same environment is also currently being evaluated for the Crew Exploration Vehicle (CEV). A significant amount of additional flammability data exists at the International Space Station (ISS) worst-case cabin conditions of 24.1% O2 at 191.4 kPa (14.7 psia). In a desire to leverage existing data, the question arises: Do materials perform similarly with respect to flammability as long as the partial pressure of oxygen remains equivalent? This question is not only relevant to NASA and space programs. In the oxygen related industry, the ability to apply existing flammability data to various manufacturing and operating conditions would be beneficial.

chunks.source: Flame Frontier Known Limits: NTRS 20160001047 (O2 partial pressure vs concentration flammability)
chunks.text: NTRS 20160001047 (O2 partial pressure vs concentration flammability) gives: ISS operating point (21% O2, 101.4 kPa; data often at 24.1% O2 from O2 fluctuations), and the finding that 21% O2 / 101.4 kPa flammability data cannot be conservatively applied to 30% O2 / 70.3 kPa. It does not give: Microgravity data: these are normal-gravity material tests (NASA-STD-6001 style). A Moon-base or rover specification.
